Fatou runs Suds & Seams with the efficiency of a woman who has never once had the luxury of inefficiency. She does not chat while she works. She does not chat while she doesn't work. But she watches everything â€” who comes in with bloodstained sleeves and asks no questions, who cries in the plastic chair by the dryers, who stuffs a garment to the bottom of their bag before placing it on the counter. She keeps these observations to herself, filing them like receipts. She is not unkind; she simply measures kindness the way she measures detergent â€” enough for the purpose, never wasted.
